Implemented in #9 (branch `fix/1-sync-state-healthy`, head `fb7c7d7`).

**What changed**
- UTF-8 on every text path: explicit `encoding="utf-8"` for the `gh`/`git` subprocess decode; stdout/stderr reconfigured to UTF-8 at CLI entry. Non-ASCII titles/bodies round-trip exactly; JSON output is never truncated by a cp1252 pipe.
- `last_error` is recorded on every failure path before propagating (the recorder covers the whole DB-touching body, including the prologue and the JSONL sidecar — lock-landing experiments drove two review rounds); unexpected crashes and pre-sync storage faults are reported as `{"ok": false}` result objects, not tracebacks.
- `status` now reports `complete` per repo, backed by a `full_sync_pending` marker: an interrupted full sync reads `complete: false`; the resuming clean run stamps `last_full_sync_at`.
- Repo slugs are canonical lowercase at three boundaries (sync write, CLI dispatch, query layer) — `--repo ZaxbyHub/X` and `zaxbyhub/x` are one repo everywhere.
- `PRAGMA user_version` migration framework (forward-only, per-migration transactions, refuses newer versions); migration 1→2 adds the marker column and case-folds + merges existing case-split databases in place.

**How to use it**
Nothing new to learn: `status` first (the bundled skill now says so), `sync` when no corpus exists. All existing commands work unchanged; output is now always UTF-8.

**Migration steps**
None required. The first command that opens an existing database upgrades it in place (one-time write; a read like `search` may perform it). Legacy rows that never recorded a full sync read `complete: false` and self-heal on the next clean sync. Already-garbled text from pre-fix cp1252 syncs is not repaired by this change — re-run `sync --force` for those; counting them is #2's `doctor`. The read-only `sql` command never migrates.

Verification: 91 tests green (baseline 70), all ten frozen acceptance checks replayed PASS, three-model review (plan critic ×5 rounds, implementation reviewer ×3 rounds with mutation probes, final critic with an independent mutation probe) — evidence and the checkpoint anchor receipt are in the PR body.

Delivered via PR #10 (head ac290278b22f331d3456188abe47895415b7b26f, branch `fix/2-worktree-global-store`; CI green on windows-latest + ubuntu-latest x Python 3.11/3.12).

## What changed

- **The graph is keyed by repo, not by checkout.** Resolution order: `--db` > `ZAXBYGRAPH_DB` > the user-level store `<root>/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/history.db` (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\zaxbygraph` on Windows / `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/zaxbygraph` elsewhere, `ZAXBYGRAPH_HOME` overrides) > a legacy in-repo DB under the main worktree (migration continuity) > the would-be store path. Every worktree, clone, and subagent of a repo now resolves the same graph.
- **Reads stop creating empty ones.** All nine read commands open read-only, never create, and when no corpus exists for the resolved repo they exit **3** with the resolved path and the exact `zaxbygraph sync --repo <slug>` command. A DB holding other repos exits **2** and lists them; a pre-#9 mixed-case legacy DB gets an actionable "same repo with pre-fold casing → `doctor --consolidate`" message.
- **Every read is repo-scoped by default** (`--repo` > git origin; `--repo ''` stays an explicit no-filter). `sql` result rows carrying a `repo` column are filtered to the resolved repo.
- **Sync lock**: `<db>.sync.lock` — a second sync joins with `{ok: true, joined: true}` and zero GitHub calls; `--wait` blocks; dead same-host holders are recovered atomically; foreign-host locks are never stolen.
- **New `where`**: prints the full resolution chain (cwd → git common dir → slug → DB path → exists/items/watermark/complete, legacy DBs found, the serving DB, sync-lock holder).
- **New `doctor [--consolidate] [--scan DIR]`**: reports scattered legacy DBs (per-DB item + garbled-row counts); `--consolidate` copies the freshest complete corpus into the store — originals are never modified (v1/mixed-case candidates are migrated on a temp copy; repo values case-folded on adoption).

## How to use it

No flags needed for the normal flow: `zaxbygraph status` in any checkout of a repo answers identically; `zaxbygraph where` shows which DB you are reading and why; `zaxbygraph doctor` reports (and `--consolidate` adopts) the old scattered DBs.

## Migration

No migration required for correctness — existing in-repo DBs keep working via the legacy fallback, and `sync` upgrades in place. To consolidate scattered DBs into the new store (the maintainer's 17-DB situation), run once per repo, e.g.:

```bash
zaxbygraph doctor --consolidate --repo OWNER/REPO --scan ~/.zmem/zaxbygraph/OWNER/REPO
```

Originals are copied, never deleted. Behavior changes to note: `status` on a fresh path now exits 3 (was empty-JSON exit 0); the store lives outside the repo, so `history.db` no longer appears under checkouts.

PR: https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/pull/11 (feat: one self-describing JSON envelope for every command, errors included)

**What changed** — every command's JSON output is now one self-describing envelope `{ok, db, repo, freshness{synced_at, age_s, complete}, data, truncated}` (+ `error{code, message, hint?}` on failures). Errors answer on **stdout** in JSON mode with coded errors (`no_such_column` carries a hint listing the real columns; probe is PRAGMA-free), while stderr keeps the one-line `error:` echo and gains an identity line (`# db=… repo=… items=… synced=… complete=…`) on every successful read. New: `zaxbygraph schema [TABLE]` (live DDL + per-column notes), `--format jsonl|compact`, `--fields a,b`, `sql --rows objects|array` + `--limit`, `item N --max-body-chars N`. `export-graph`/`sync`/`doctor`/`where` converged on the same emitter. Exit codes (0/1/2/3), the read-only SQL safety layers, and the DB schema are unchanged.

**How to use** — parse stdout as JSON and branch on `ok`; the payload you used to get at the top level is under `data`. Stream safely with `--format jsonl` (any `head -n` prefix parses). Discover the schema with `zaxbygraph schema [TABLE]` instead of a doc path.

**Migration** (breaking by design — the issue's decided hard switch, v0.2.0): move top-level payload reads under `data` (`data["ok"]` keeps working — `ok` is promoted to the envelope root for every command, including `sync`); `churn`/`open` payloads are arrays under `data`; pass `--rows array` to `sql` if you need the old positional rows; switch stderr-parsing error handling to reading `ok`/`error.code` from stdout.

**Delivered: PR #12 — https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/pull/12** (Workstream B, PR 1 of 1 of epic #8)

**What changed**
- `search` now answers natural-language queries: tokens are porter-stemmed (`reconnect` finds `reconnection`), ranked by bm25 (title-weighted 10/1/3, recency tie-break), and comment hits merge into their parent item (`matching_comments` + `comment_snippet`) instead of a separate unranked list.
- AND→OR fallback: when the strict all-tokens pass finds fewer hits than the page, the query retries with stopwords removed and tokens OR-joined; `matched_mode` reports which pass produced the page.
- `total_matches` + `corpus_items` distinguish "no hits in N items" from an empty corpus; `index_stale` flags a database that predates the schema (reads never migrate).
- Schema v2→v3: both FTS tables rebuild in place with the porter tokenizer on the next `sync` — no resync; the migration rolls back whole on failure (regression-tested).

**How to use** — unchanged: `zaxbygraph search "memory leak in websocket reconnect"`. Shape change (v0.3.0): the separate `comments` list is gone (comment hits are items now).

**Migration** — no action required: the first `sync` after upgrade rebuilds the FTS index in place (seconds at ~3k items). Until then, `search` reports `index_stale: true`. Once migrated, older zaxbygraph builds refuse the database (forward-only schema).

Full trace: 8 frozen acceptance checks (6 RED→GREEN at base `4789858`), 158-test suite green, three independent review/critic approvals. Checkpoint anchor receipts: [pre-implementation](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/4#issuecomment-5969956751).

PR: #13 — feat: cold sync stops exhausting the rate limit and losing the listing

**What changed**

- The issues listing now streams one page per `gh` call and commits each
  page as it arrives, so a mid-listing 502/rate limit keeps every page
  already delivered together with its watermark — the next run resumes
  instead of restarting the corpus from zero (AC1).
- New default `--source graphql`: one aliased GraphQL query per listing
  page replaces the old ~5 REST calls per PR (comments, reviews, review
  comments, files, pull details); connections that overflow their page are
  flagged and completed through the per-item REST fallback (AC2/AC3).
  `--source rest` keeps the plain REST source. Patches always come from
  REST, so `--include-patches` still works.
- Rate limits are budgeted, not fatal: an exhausted core limit is slept out
  until the reported reset and retried; the window is reported as
  `rate_limit_remaining` / `rate_limit_reset_at` in the sync result and in
  `status` (new `sync_state` columns, schema v4) (AC4).
- After a completed full sync, a source deletion oracle marks stored items
  gone as `deleted`/`transferred` (rows kept, `fetch_log` trail); a 404/410
  on an item's own fetch marks it deleted too (AC5).

**How to use it**

`zaxbygraph sync --repo OWNER/REPO` — same command as before; GraphQL is
the default source. Add `--source rest` for the old behavior. No migration
action is needed for existing databases (schema v3→v4 applies automatically
on the next sync; the new columns are diagnostic).

**Evidence**

Eight frozen acceptance checks (authored independently before the fix,
proven RED on main and GREEN on this branch), full suite 188 tests OK, a
live two-source parity smoke against real GitHub (identical corpora;
GraphQL ~4.4× faster wall time on this repo), independent reviewer and
final-critic approvals. Full closure evidence in the PR body; trace
artifacts in `.agents/issue-traces/5-cold-sync-rate-limit-and-listing-loss/`.

No migration required. Merge is gated on maintainer approval.

PR opened: https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/pull/14 — "what closed #N from timeline links, with provenance on every edge" (head e2e13ba962b57c447eb739da0174953fb6829b14).

**What changed** (schema v5): edges carry a `source` provenance column inside the unique key (`keyword` / `timeline` / `closing_ref` / `payload`); keyword closing links renamed to `closes_keyword`; `closes` is now backed by timeline `closed` events and PR `closingIssuesReferences`; new relations `cross_referenced` (repo-qualified for foreign sources), `closed_by_commit`, `merged_commit`, `merged_by`, `reverts` — so "what closed #N" is answerable from merge-commit auto-close, UI links, and timeline cross-references, and the graph joins to `git log` via `commit:<sha>` nodes.

**How to use**: `zaxbygraph sync` as usual — `item N` / `related N` edges now carry `source`; `path` traverses the new relations; `sql` can filter `WHERE source = 'timeline'`. Existing v4 databases migrate automatically on the next sync (forward-only, ids/counts preserved). Migration: automatic; no flags change. A v4 database read before its next sync reports `index_stale` in search results — run a sync to migrate.

**Boundaries disclosed in the PR body**: REST-only syncs (`--source rest`) capture no timeline/closing-ref edges (GraphQL page query only); timelines beyond 500 events retain the newest 500 with a `fetch_log` note; timeline/closing_ref edges are append-only across degraded re-ingests.

What changed (Workstream D, the last epic-#8 workstream):
- `zaxbygraph mcp` — a stdio MCP server, hand-written stdlib JSON-RPC 2.0 (zero runtime dependencies, per AC7 + the repo's no-dependencies invariant; the SDK-extra alternative stays open in the PR body for a maintainer veto). 11 typed tools (`graph_status`, `search`, `get_item`, `related`, `path`, `pr_overlap`, `file_history`, `what_closed`, `open_items`, `sql`, `sync`), each answering with the Workstream A JSON envelope including structured errors with hints. - Repo resolution without a cwd: explicit `repo` argument → server `--repo/--db` pin → MCP roots → server cwd git origin — the same slug-keyed store the CLI resolves, so worktrees share one graph and reads never create.
- Stale reads answer immediately and start ONE locked background sync (`freshness.refreshing: true`; threshold `--stale-seconds`, default 900). `sync` never blocks — job id + `graph_status` progress.
- The three proven hand-written queries become first-class on both surfaces: `pr_overlap`/`file_history`/`what_closed` tools + `overlap`/`file-history`/`what-closed` commands.

For a per-slug store (one repo per DB) this is a harmless no-op, but this PR explicitly keeps multi-repo legacy DBs reachable via `--db` for migration continuity. In that case, a query like `SELECT repo, number FROM items` on a DB whose first `limit` rows belong to other repos can return far fewer rows than exist for the resolved repo — or none — while `truncated` is still reported as `true`, which is misleading. Since the repo can't be pushed into arbitrary user SQL, consider at least recomputing/qualifying `truncated` after the filter (e.g. only report it when the post-filter slice is actually full) so callers aren't told there is more data when the filter already discarded the rest.

**Bug found while dogfooding this branch (head `e2e13ba9`): `_timeline_selection` emits a brace-unbalanced query, which breaks every sync whose page touches an item needing timeline continuation.**

Reproduction (installed from this branch; `zaxbygraph sync --repo zaxbyhub/opencode-swarm`):

```
error: gh: Expected one of SCHEMA, SCALAR, TYPE, ENUM, INPUT, UNION, INTERFACE, actual: RCURLY ("}") at [1, 716]
```

Root cause: in `src/zaxbygraph/graphql.py`, the `_timeline_selection(args)` template's final line

```python
" ... on PullRequest { number repository { nameWithOwner } } } } } } }"
```

carries **one extra closing brace** — the rendered selection is brace-balance −1 (the static `_TIMELINE_NODES` block used by the chunk query is balanced, which is why only the `_timeline_page`/`_complete_timeline` continuation path breaks). The over-closed query makes GitHub's parser expect a type name and hit `}` — position 716 with a real cursor.

Verified fix: drop one `}` from that line's tail. After the one-character fix:

- `_timeline_selection("first: 50")` balance: **0** (was −1); `_timeline_page` full query balance: **0**; chunk query unchanged at 0.
- Live `gh api graphql` with the fixed query returns real data (e.g. `p3087.timelineItems.totalCount = 3`).

P3: The reverse title-revert pass is not symmetric with the forward span normalization in extract.py. Forward: for a revert title it strips the closing quote and whitespace from the span before the exact-title lookup. Reverse: it matches stored titles verbatim against `Revert "<title>"` / `Revert "<title>`. A target title with trailing whitespace therefore never completes its revert edge (forward recognizes `Revert "T "`, reverse never generates that variant), and a target title ending in `"` (e.g. `Foo"`) generates variant `Revert "Foo"`, which the forward semantics attribute to title `Foo` — so the reverse pass can attach a legacy revert PR to the wrong target. Normalize the span (strip trailing quote then whitespace) when generating reversed variants instead of using the title verbatim.

**What changed.** `zaxbygraph export-corpus` writes a deterministic, hash-stamped JSONL snapshot of one store (`zaxbygraph.corpus.v1`): a manifest line (counts, `corpus_sha256`, store completeness, an unhashed `provenance` block), one canonical-JSON line per item (each with a `content_hash`) and per release, an optional `revisions` line (`--include revisions`), and an `orphan_edges` trailer.
